A third '''moon''' [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="atlas" /> alongside [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]<ref name="DB-Nass, Boss">{{DB|character|bossnass|Nass, Boss}}</ref> and [[Rori/Legends|Rori]].<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> It did not have a name and was in fact little more than an overgrown [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]].<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The first mention of the third moon of Naboo is in ''[[Secrets of Naboo]]'',<ref name="SoN">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> a reference book written by [[Steve Miller]] and [[J.D. Wiker]] and illustrated by [[Matt Busch]], [[Albert Yu]] and [[Kurt Kaufman]] and released on [[February]], [[2001]].

In the [[2003]] [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], the three moons of Naboo could be seen from the surface. However, none of the moons were specifically identified from this vantage point. In the [[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed|''Jump to Lightspeed'']] expansion pack released in [[2004]], the three moons of Naboo could be seen from space. One of these moons was identified as Rori in the [[Star Wars Galaxies Memory Book|''Star Wars Galaxies'' Memory Book]], but it is not known which of the other two moons was Ohma-D'un. The [[Star Wars video games|game]], developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], was shut down on [[December 15]], [[2011]].
